title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
lede: Nari Labs released NariQ quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B at 3, 2.5 and 2 bits per weight, and reports that the 3-bit and 2.5-bit files hold BF16 quality on agent tasks, math and vision.

points: NariQ is a trellis-coded post-training quantization, calibrated on real coding-agent traces and building on QTIP.
On DeepSWE, BF16 scores 39.8 against 41.0 at 3 bits and 41.9 at 2.5 bits; the 2-bit file falls to 28.6.
The files need Nari's llama.cpp fork; stock llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio cannot load them yet.
The fork targets SM120 cards like the RTX PRO 6000; an M3 Pro decodes about 3.8 tokens a second, and pre-Ampere GPUs fall back to CPU.
Only the language model is quantized; KV-cache and activation quantization come next. The files are Apache-2.0.

points.text: A skeptic of benchmark-tuned quants credits the release for testing held-out, long-horizon tasks beyond coding.
Some suspect the harness explains the gains; the author replies that BF16 in their harness lands close to Unsloth's reported DeepSWE figure.
Mac users ask whether it fits a 16 GB machine, and a reply says 3.8 tokens a second is too slow to iterate with.
One commenter reads NariQ as a derivative of exl3's codebook and wants that lineage stated up front.
